text:
alice_support: Hey @customer_mrt 

We got your ticket about truncated SSE responses. Can you drop the exact client trace + request id?

customer_mrt: request_id: r-9f8e7d6c5b. Repro is simple: we stream a ~6k token response, and the client receives the last data: event but no trailing metadata. The JSON payload ends with an extra comma and then stream closes. Happens through Fastly in front of the edge.

curl --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXXX" \\  \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-xxl","prompt":"<very long prompt...>"}' \\  \\
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/streams/generate

Observed tail from client tcpdump:

data: {"id":"tok_983","chunk":"...closing thoughts","tokens":["closing"," thoughts",]}

(Notice the trailing comma after last token; client JSON parse fails. No finish_reason seen.)

customer_mrt: Node sse client prints: "parse error: unexpected token at end of input" then connection closed. Curl exits 52.

alice_support: Thanks. @jon_runtime @emma_sre can you take a look? Customer says Fastly sits in front and may be clipping last bytes.

jon_runtime: On it. Two hypotheses: 1) upstream (runtime) wrote final chunk but Fastly/edge normalized/chunked the body and dropped the terminal bytes during a midstream buffer flush; 2) TLS session terminated early by Fastly healthcheck or by an intermediate WAF that enforces a max buffered body size and truncates. Need raw envoy/runtime logs and Fastly side logs.

emma_sre: I pulled edge logs for r-9f8e7d6c5b. Fastly returned 200 from origin but with response length shorter than content-length our origin reported; we see a downstream RST after ~33s. Fastly log excerpt:

FASTLY vcl_log: origin_response_body_size=5172 origin_status=200 client_close=1 downstream_rst=1

We also see a worker abort: "body_too_large" in a cached service configuration 2025-10-30.

carlos_eng: If Fastly is configured to buffer the entire response before streaming to the client (they can), and they have a limit, they might cut the final chunk if that buffer hits a threshold. That would leave the last bytes missing and no finish_reason. Two immediate options: 1) have origin set Transfer-Encoding: chunked and disable buffering (Cache-Control: no-transform) so Fastly can stream; 2) include final metadata inline with last data frame to avoid depending on a separate trailing frame.

customer_mrt: We don't control Fastly config. Our customers route through their CDN. Any short-term client workarounds?

jon_runtime: Client-side mitigation: 1) tolerate trailing-comma or partial JSON by attempting to reconnect with a resume token; 2) detect incomplete JSON and call the resume endpoint with ?resume_from=last_tok_id; 3) request smaller response windows via max_tokens param. We can add server-side support for an "inline final metadata" flag that bundles finish_reason in the last data event (same event).

alice_support: I'm drafting a KB note about "CDN buffering and streaming". Also escalating to CDN partnerships to document required Fastly settings.

emma_sre: For root cause, I'm seeing origin emitted final_chunk and then wrote a trailing SSE comment and metadata, but fastly worker aborted write due to body_toobig threshold triggered by a misconfigured fastly VCL for certain customers. Origin logs show:

[origin] emit_event seq=201 bytes=4800 req=r-9f8e7d6c5b
[origin] emit_event seq=202 bytes=120 final=true req=r-9f8e7d6c5b
[origin] emit_event seq=203 bytes=34 meta{"finish_reason":"length"}

Then fastly entry shows downstream_rst. So origin did send final metadata. Not delivered.

carlos_eng: Ok, next steps:
- Runtime: implement an opt-in header X-RW-STREAM-BUNDLE-FINAL that instructs server to merge final metadata into previous data event. Low risk and backwards compatible.
- Platform/SRE: reach out to CDN customers about disabling full-response buffering for streaming endpoints or bumping FP body limits.
- Support: provide customer with client-side robust JSON concat logic snippet.

jon_runtime: I'll open a PR to encode final metadata inside the same event payload by default for a while, so clients get finish_reason atomically. Also instrument runtime to emit metric 'sse.incomplete_deliveries' when origin sees downstream close before confirmation.

alice_support: Customer asked about billing impact (any extra tokens counted twice if client reconnects?).

jon_runtime: If the client reconnects and requests a resume, by default the runtime will deduplicate tokens emitted server-side using token ids; billing is charged on tokens generated, not tokens delivered, so there shouldn't be double billing. We'll add explicit note in billing docs and a header X-RW-RESUME-DEDUPE=true on resume responses.

customer_mrt: Can you share a quick Node snippet to try the reconnect approach?

alice_support: Sure, here's a short sketch (informal):

```
// pseudo-code
let lastId = null;
function handleEvent(data) {
  try {
    const obj = JSON.parse(data);
    lastId = obj.id || lastId;
    applyTokens(obj.tokens);
  } catch(e) {
    // truncated JSON -> reconnect and request resume
    fetch('/v1/streams/generate?resume_from=' + lastId, {headers:{Authorization:'Bearer ...'}})
      .then(stream => pipe(stream))
  }
}
```

jon_runtime: We'll ship the 'bundle-final' header behind a feature flag in staging today. SRE will test with a Fastly-configured test app to confirm final metadata arrives when buffering is disabled.

emma_sre: I'll also add an edge alert: if origin reports emit_event final but downstream closed within 5s, raise an incident and increment sse.truncated_fastly metric so we can track per-customer.

customer_mrt: Appreciate the quick triage. Any ETA?

alice_support: Plan: staging flag by EOD, 1-2 day rollout after Fastly test. Meanwhile use client resume logic. I'll keep you in this thread with the PR link.

streaming-bot: Created ticket RW-8001 for feature flag 'bundle-final-metadata' and RW-8002 for edge alerting.

alice_support: Thanks everyone. Closing loop once staging validated. :white_check_mark:

customer_mrt: Thanks, will try resume hack and report back.
